caseStudy.problem: A production Java platform combines established Jakarta EE and Payara services with an ongoing move toward smaller Quarkus services. Changes have to account for live operational behavior, cloud dependencies, and on-call support.
work: Maintain and improve Jakarta EE and Payara backend services.
Contribute to the move from legacy workloads toward Quarkus-based services.
Build Java, SQL, asynchronous, and AWS integrations while supporting incidents, performance analysis, and on-call rotations.
decisions: Modernize incrementally so changes can be introduced alongside a running production platform.
Use asynchronous communication where services need to remain decoupled, while keeping integration behavior explicit.
Treat deployment, code quality, and operational support as part of the implementation.
caseStudy.impact: Modernization stays connected to the behavior and constraints of the existing platform. Findings from production support also provide concrete input for stability and performance work.

caseStudy.problem: An enterprise Spring Boot backend needed new functionality within a larger system, plus dependable communication with internal services and external file and cloud integrations.
work: Took responsibility for an epic within the backend and implemented its Spring Boot services.
Integrated Kafka, OpenFeign, SFTP services, and AWS S3.
Worked with Business Analysts and QA, deployed development and QA environments, documented APIs, and supported incident analysis.
decisions: Use Kafka for asynchronous flows and OpenFeign for direct service-to-service calls.
Keep SFTP and S3 integrations behind backend boundaries instead of exposing their details to callers.
Document API behavior so development and QA shared the same contract.
caseStudy.impact: Backend changes moved through development and QA with their integrations, documentation, and support context in place. The same ownership continued into incident analysis and legacy maintenance.

caseStudy.problem: An existing business application needed to move toward an Angular and Spring Boot implementation while preserving the behavior users and downstream processes already relied on.
work: Documented the existing interface and backend behavior before rebuilding it.
Recreated the frontend in Angular and the backend flow in Spring Boot.
Moved logic from database procedures into the application layer.
decisions: Capture current behavior before changing technology, reducing ambiguity during the migration.
Separate frontend and backend responsibilities between Angular and Spring Boot.
Translate database procedure logic into application code that could be reviewed and maintained with the service.
caseStudy.impact: The migration produced an application-layer version of the existing behavior and reduced how much business logic remained tied to database procedures.
